analyst_view.overall: Early view: Union Saint-Gilloise (4th, 10 points) are unbeaten in Europe and in the Belgian league, and host Lech Poznan at Den Dreef in Leuven with a top-eight place within reach. Lech have one point and 12 goals conceded in four games, and were winless in six in all competitions after losing 3-1 at Benfica.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. Union have scored ten and conceded two in this league phase and Lech's away games ended 0-4 and 1-3, so a comfortable home win fits. I stay with the number: Union are efficient rather than wasteful, which caps how high this goes.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.2 corners. Union had only one corner at Celta because they sat back and countered, but at home against a weak side they will have much more of the ball, so the two balance out near the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. Union's win at Celta was clean and Lech's defeat at Benfica was not a bad-tempered game either, so a one-sided match with few bookings fits.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.8 shots, 21.3 of them for Union. I lean lower: David Hubert's side are efficient rather than high-volume (eight shots in the 2-1 win at Celta, with Besfort Zeneli scoring twice) and tend to manage games once ahead. Lech will concede chances, but around 26 looks more realistic.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.6 shots on target, which is very high. Benfica found plenty of openings against Lech, so they can be opened up, but Union's measured style points to a total nearer 9 or 10.
